key_insight: TomoTransformer reframes sparse-view CT reconstruction as a flexible token-based view-interpolation problem, enabling a single model to handle variable angles, projection counts, and detector sizes without retraining.
clinical_relevance: This could make CT reconstruction more robust and scalable across scanners and protocols, potentially reducing the need for task-specific model retraining in real-world imaging workflows.
method: Represents each local filtered projection as a token in a transformer.
Uses self-attention in back-projection space to infer missing views.
Designed to accept arbitrary input/target angles and detector dimensions.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on a large-scale mixed dataset and, across multiple benchmark sparse-view datasets, outperformed or matched strong baselines including ViewTrans, with zero-shot success on experimental nanoscale brain synchrotron data.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on how well real scanner geometries and data distributions match the training setup, so external validation and integration testing remain important.
paper_title: TomoTransformer: Towards a Foundation Model for CT Reconstruction
